outcome: Coordinate briefs, assets, crews, edits, approvals and distribution to reduce production delay and rework without weakening creative control.
overview: Production teams still coordinate briefs, crews, assets, edits and approvals through email and spreadsheets, so versions go missing, approvals are hard to evidence and cost visibility arrives only after the fact. This solution puts one orchestrated workflow behind the whole path from brief to publish: schedules and resources are planned in one place, ingested assets are checked against rights and deliverable specifications, edit and legal approvals are routed by role with separation of duties, and publishing runs through an immutable version gate with rollback. An 8–12 week pilot on a single format targets shorter cycle time and less rework, leaving creative judgement exactly where it is.

benefits.text: Reduce production cycle time and rework by a target 20% on the pilot format
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Target from the source catalogue, to validate against the customer’s own cycle-time baseline during the pilot — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Improve on-time delivery and make every approval traceable to a named role and version
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on consistent adoption of the workflow rather than side channels for urgent work

benefits.text: Cut wrong-version and missing-deliverable errors by gating publish on immutable versions and specification checks
benefits.source: Architecture design — the publish gate rejects assets failing version, rights or deliverable checks
benefits.limits: Covers only assets published through the governed workflow; manual distribution paths remain unprotected

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); briefs, assets, approvals and cost records remain in the customer tenancy in the reference designs

notFor.situation: There is no agreed brief-to-publish process to orchestrate
notFor.why: Workflow automation encodes an existing agreed process; automating a contested one multiplies the disagreement rather than resolving it

notFor.situation: Asset and project systems cannot be integrated during the engagement
notFor.why: The value comes from joining brief, schedule, asset and approval state; a workflow layer with no systems beneath it is another silo

notFor.situation: Automated publishing without approval gates is the goal
notFor.why: Separation of duties and named approval before publish are structural to the design; removing them removes the control the record claims

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns the production process, the approval matrix and every publish decision · Duration: 8–12 week PoV; further 16–26 weeks to multi-format rollout
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, integration engineer, media-workflow engineer; customer production-operations owner, post-production lead, legal reviewer, security approver · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Discovery and baseline agreement
2) Process definition and approval-matrix sign-off
3) System integration and workflow build
4) Exception, rollback and failure-mode testing
5) Training, runbooks and controlled rollout on the pilot format
6) Stabilisation and handover

Publish rollback demonstrated on a live-like deliverable
Security review passed and production UAT complete
